history: always-repro'd across v1.4.1907..v1.9.2607 (all 20 bisectable releases probed linearly under both predicates; no invalid probes). v1.4.1907 is the bisection floor, so this means 'for as long as it is checkable'. The 2021-02-04 report is nonetheless covered: v1.5.2010 (2020-10-22) predates it and reproduces. Not an NDEBUG artefact -- the symptom is a diagnostic from a Release-built validator, not an assert.
summary: Still fails on main (1.9.0.5433, 13730886e) and on all 20 bisectable releases v1.4.1907..v1.9.2607 -- probed linearly under two predicates, 42 probes, all exit 0x80004005, no invalid probes; none of the 20 measured release binaries compiled it, and v1.4.1907 (2019-07) is the floor. The merged pointer is not ambiguous: with -Vd the compile succeeds and both phi float addrspace(3)* have every incoming value GEPing the SAME global. lib/DxilValidation/DxilValidation.cpp (~L3820-3849) walks GEP/bitcast chains only when the instruction is itself a GEP or bitcast, so any other TGSM-pointer-typed instruction, phi included, is rejected without its operands being examined; dxv.exe built from this tree rejects the module too, so it is the in-tree validator and not only the redistributable dxil.dll. All five optimization levels were captured on main: -Od and -O0 compile clean, -O1, -O2 and -O3 all fail, so the reporter's workaround costs all optimization and not just -O3. At -O0 no phi of groupshared pointers is formed at all, which is why it escapes. CAUTION for anyone re-running this: v1.4.1907 emits the same rule with no "error: " prefix and an instruction address instead of a source line:column, and -O1/-O2 name the phis differently from -O3, so a predicate carrying the prefix or the instruction text scores reproducing probes as no-repro -- one such predicate faked a transition at v1.5.2010. Whether the walk should accept a merge whose operands all resolve to one global, or the optimizer should not form it, is a maintainer decision this triage does not make.
title: DXC Validation Error: TGSM pointers must originate from an unambiguous TGSM global variable
